newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN boss to be removed next wk - gvt source.
newsitem.headline: GAN boss to be removed next wk - gvt source.

text.p: GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, who has refused a government call for him to resign, will be removed by decree next week, a government source said on Tuesday.
"There will be a decree ending his mandate," said the source.
This would be done at a cabinet meeting next Wednesday and was normal procedure in the case where the head of a state company did not resign at the government's request.
The name of a replacement was likely to be decided the same day, the source added.
The government called for Bonnaud's resignation on Monday after the collapse of attempts to privatise GAN bank subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC).

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said last week that he was abandoning a tender for the sale of 67 percent of CIC after receiving only one eligible offer, from BNP, and he said Bonnaud as well as CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt had not helped to promote the sell-off.

The source declined to suggest likely names to take over from Bonnaud, whose successor is also set to name a replacement for Yoncourt at the head of CIC, a grouping of 11 regional banks whose sale was seen as a prerequisite to privatising insurance company parent Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN).
